title: Checkpoint: What Money Is
objective: After this level you can trace money from barter and coins to digital money, and explain what gives it value.
summary: Useful money is durable, portable, divisible, uniform, limited in supply and acceptable. From shells to bitcoin, every money has rested on trust.

cards.headline: Shells, stones, coins, paper, records, code. Which makes the best money?
cards.body: Chapter 1 has walked you through money in all its costumes. Economists have a scorecard for judging them. Time to use it.

cards.headline: The six-trait test
cards.body: Useful money is durable (it lasts), portable (easy to carry), divisible (splits into small amounts), uniform (each unit is as good as another), limited in supply (hard to make more of) and acceptable (people take it). That last one is Level 6's whole story: acceptance rests on trust.

items.label: Yap stones
points: Not portable: the biggest are over 3.5 m wide

items.label: A US $20 bill
points: Scores well on all six traits

cards.headline: One thread from shells to code
cards.body: Money kept changing shape: shells and salt, Lydia's stamped coins, China's paper, gold-backed notes, bank records, bitcoin's blockchain. What stayed the same were Level 1's three jobs, and the thing under them all: people accept money because they trust others will too. Money works because people believe it will.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 complete
learned: Money does three jobs: pay, measure, save
From shells and coins to paper, records and code
Its value rests on trust and acceptance

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT one of the six traits of useful money?

options.label: Durable enough to last
options.rationale: Durability is on the list: money has to last.

options.label: Easy to carry around
options.rationale: Portability is on the list: money has to be easy to carry.

options.label: Splits into small amounts
options.rationale: Divisibility is on the list: money has to split into small amounts.

questions.explanation: The six traits are durability, portability, divisibility, uniformity, limited supply and acceptability. Material isn't one of them.

questions.prompt: A country's only banknote is worth a whole year's pay. Which trait does it fail?

options.label: Durability
options.rationale: A banknote can last fine. The problem is splitting it.

options.label: Acceptability
options.rationale: People might accept it; they just can't use it for small things.

questions.explanation: Money has to split into small amounts for everyday buying. One giant note fails divisibility.

questions.prompt: From Level 1: you put $20 in a drawer to spend next month. Which job is that money doing?

options.label: Medium of exchange
options.rationale: That's the job it does when you spend it.

options.label: Unit of account
options.rationale: That's the job it does when prices are quoted in it.

options.label: Double coincidence of wants
options.rationale: That's barter's matching problem, not a job of money.

questions.explanation: Keeping money to spend later is its job as a store of value.

questions.prompt: Which list is in the right order, oldest first?

options.label: Song paper notes → Lydian coins → Bitcoin → Nixon's gold decision
options.rationale: Lydia's coins came about 1,700 years before Song paper notes.

options.label: Lydian coins → Nixon's gold decision → Song paper notes → Bitcoin
options.rationale: Song paper notes (around 1023) came long before 1971.

options.label: Lydian coins → Song paper notes → Nixon's gold decision → Bitcoin
Bitcoin → Lydian coins → Song paper notes → Nixon's gold decision
options.rationale: Bitcoin is the newest of all: 2009.

questions.explanation: Lydia around 650 BCE, Song notes around 1023, Nixon in 1971, bitcoin in 2009.

questions.prompt: Across Chapter 1, what finally gives money its value?

options.label: The precious metal it's made of
options.rationale: Today's money is paper and records, backed by no metal.

options.label: How hard it is to print or mint
options.rationale: A $100 bill costs about 11 cents to print.

options.label: Trust that others will accept it
A fixed link to gold in a vault

questions.explanation: From Yap's stones to fiat dollars, money works because people trust that others will accept it.
